verdict.rationale: Rainforest documents three seller-onboarding paths: an embeddable Merchant Onboarding Component (recommended), the Platform Portal, and a direct API with a create-merchant endpoint. It also runs KYC/KYB verification and validates bank accounts through Plaid. Direct API submission of sensitive data is limited to platforms Rainforest has approved, and terms acceptance is never documented. missing for 10: documented terms-of-service acceptance capture, a true hosted/redirect onboarding flow for sellers (the portal is for platforms entering data on merchants' behalf), unrestricted direct-API access, independent corroboration

support.subject: As a developer, I can onboard a seller through the API — KYB and KYC, bank account linking, and terms acceptance — with hosted flows and embeddable components when I don't want to build the forms

citations.quote: Rainforest offers three options to onboard merchants: **Merchant Onboarding Component (Recommended)**... **Rainforest Platform Portal**... **Rainforest API**
Create a merchant with an initial merchant application.
Platforms that are approved by Rainforest can send sensitive merchant onboarding data, including bank accounts and Social Security Numbers, to Rainforest via a direct to API integration.

Rainforest performs the Know Your Customer (KYC) and Know Your Business (KYB) verifications requirement by the card brands and provides you with an approved, declined, or manual review response within minutes.
Rainforest utilizes a third-party partner, Plaid, for real-time validation.
Utilizing our embedded component or API, submit for real-time onboarding processing payments in minutes.
